referents.why: 'say to him': the him is Pharaoh, to whom Moses is sent (cl2, before Pharaoh).
in the quoted words spoken by the LORD, 'my people' is the LORD's own; first person in God's speech refers to the speaker.
referents.category: first person inside a divine speech

referents.why: 'that they may serve me' is in the LORD's quoted words; first person is the speaker, the LORD.
referents.category: first person inside a divine speech

referents.why: 'rise early' is a command to Moses, the addressee of God's speech.
'present yourself before Pharaoh' is a command to Moses.
'you will say to him' is addressed to Moses, who is to deliver the message.
referents.category: implied subject of a commanded saying

referents.why: 'let my people go' is said to Pharaoh, the addressee of the LORD's words; second masculine singular.
referents.category: implied addressee of a quoted command

referents.why: 'that they may serve me' has a plural subject; the people (w27) is the collective that the command concerns and the only candidate of that sense.
referents.category: collective subject of a purpose clause

links.why: cl3 is inside God's speech and cl0 is its frame, which comes first; a then-link back to the frame is backward and crosses the speech boundary.
waw joining two commands at one level; the conjunction supports it.
weqatal 'you will say' continues whatever it follows, the clause about Pharaoh going out.
an imperative followed by waw + a yiqtol in a different person is a purpose, not a plain and (rule for purpose).
'let my people go, so that they may serve me': command, then waw + yiqtol in third person plural, which looks forward to the aim.
God says, and the first thing said is a collection of commands joined by waw (R1).
'you will say to him' is a saying clause; what is said is the frame 'thus says the LORD' of the innermost speech (R1).
links.category: speech content of a commanded saying

links.why: 'thus says the LORD' introduces a collection of commands with its aim; content points at the imperative group (R1).

groups.why: God (the LORD) speaks to Moses; the commanded turn for Moses to deliver is nested as a part, and the setting clause cl3-cl4 sits in God's speech.
groups.category: outer speech with nested commanded turn

groups.why: 'rise early' and 'present yourself' are commands joined by waw at one level, one group with two command members; 'part' is not an imperative role.
Moses is commanded to say the LORD's words to Pharaoh, so the commanded turn is spoken by Moses (R2) and holds the quoted turn as its part.
groups.category: commanded turn holding the quoted words

groups.why: the innermost turn is the LORD's quoted words to Pharaoh, so the sender is the LORD; the builder had no addressee and the part is the imperative group.
'let my people go' with its aim, 'that they may serve me'; the aim is an imperative role, the builder's part is not.

none_fit.where: cl3 and cl4 (hinneh with a participle: 'when Pharaoh goes out to the water')
none_fit.what: a temporal 'when' clause setting the time of the commanded act; no link type expresses a temporal clause (when_if_though is for fronted ki only).
a bare participle clause ('when Pharaoh goes out to the water') giving the time of the command that follows; no link type states a temporal setting.

none_fit.where: cl3 and cl4 (hinneh 'there' plus a bare participle, 'when Pharaoh goes out to the water')
none_fit.what: A temporal clause setting the time of the command in cl2. No link type covers a when-clause that is neither a condition nor a nested role, so it is left unlinked.

cant_tell.what: whether the when-clause cl3-cl4 belongs to God's speech or to Moses's commanded turn
cant_tell.why: it is God's instruction about the time, so it is placed in turn0; the text does not mark which speech the setting belongs to.

cant_tell.what: whether the setting cl3 and cl4 belong to the LORD's words or to Moses's delivery
cant_tell.why: the second person and the sequence put them in the LORD's speech to Moses, so they are parts of the outer turn; recorded because the setting could be read as Moses's own timing.
